commits.message: update the css for the dl dt

findings.title: High CSS selector repetition and specificity
findings.description: The new CSS rules repeat the same 5 selector patterns across 7 different rule blocks (88 lines total). Each rule block targets: table.wfacp_mini_cart_items, .wfacp_order_summary_container, .wfacp_collapsible_order_summary_wrap, .wfacp_mb_mini_cart_wrap, and .wfacp_mini_cart_start_h. This creates maintenance burden and increases file size.
findings.fix_suggestion: Consider using CSS custom properties (variables) or a shared class approach. Alternatively, use a CSS preprocessor mixin or consolidate selectors where possible. The repeated selector pattern could be extracted into a shared selector group.
findings.impact: Maintenance burden, larger CSS file size, potential performance impact from parsing long selectors

findings.title: Use of !important flags
findings.description: Multiple properties use !important flags (float, margin, display, clear, font-weight, width, line-height). This is acceptable for theme compatibility purposes to ensure styles work across different WordPress themes and plugins.
findings.fix_suggestion: Can be refactored in future CSS cleanup if needed, but current approach is acceptable for theme compatibility.
findings.impact: Acceptable for theme compatibility - ensures consistent styling across different themes

findings.title: Potential CSS parsing performance impact
findings.description: The extremely long selector chains (5 selectors per rule, some with pseudo-elements) may impact CSS parsing performance, especially on lower-end devices. Each selector is ~150-200 characters long.
findings.fix_suggestion: While the impact is minimal, consider if shorter, more specific class names could be added to HTML templates instead of relying on long descendant selectors. This would improve both performance and maintainability.
findings.impact: Minor CSS parsing overhead, larger file size

positive_aspects.description: All CSS rule blocks include clear comments explaining their purpose and scope ('Works for all order summary types')
The styles target all order summary container types, ensuring consistent variation display across different layouts
Includes proper clearfix patterns using ::after pseudo-elements, preventing layout issues
The new styles target different contexts (mini cart/order summary) than existing variation styles (product switcher), avoiding conflicts

recommendations.action: Consider refactoring repeated selectors into a shared pattern or CSS variable approach
recommendations.benefit: Improved maintainability and reduced file size

recommendations.action: Consider refactoring !important flags in future CSS cleanup (currently acceptable for theme compatibility)

notes: CSS-only changes for styling WooCommerce product variations in order summary. Functionality is sound, but code quality improvements could be made for better maintainability.
